end.summary:
- Practised making 10 with finger groups and spoken examples.
- Gauri gave 5+5 and 7+3 during the lesson.
- They repeatedly said 5+5 was the only way to make 10.
- The belief that 6+4 makes 10 was not corrected by the end.
- Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making 10 in different ways using fingers and examples. Gauri used 5+5 and 7+3, but kept returning to the mix-up that only 5+5 makes 10; it was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, try building 10 with two groups of buttons, starting with 5+5, then changing one button to make 4+6 and 3+7.
